description:
## Problem
Library draft PR #7 holds the framework all synthetic generators reuse (65,536-row blocks, ChaCha8 stream keyed by benchmark, table, stream, seed and block; owned sampling routines) and the SSB generator. It copies the legacy generator's row counts, and its acceptance report predates the owner's rules.

## Change
On PR #7: switch SSB to specification row counts (part = 200,000 x floor(1 + log2 SF), date = 2,556 rows, lineorder from orders x 1-7 lines per the SSB specification); implement the acceptance rules in tools/ssb_acceptance.py (min-max or 99.9% prediction interval from 5 legacy seeds, rank check for boundary quantiles on low-cardinality columns, empty-query rate rule); regenerate the report and the golden hashes; get an independent review; merge.

## Decision gates
- If the specification is ambiguous for a count (lineorder is approximate in the spec), follow the reference ssb-dbgen behaviour and state the source; if no reference is reachable, stop and ask the owner.
- If any acceptance criterion fails under the decided rules, stop and report the metric; do not tune the rule.
- Distribution comparison against legacy uses the columns whose domain is unchanged by the row-count change; list any metric excluded for that reason.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
